cards.text: Friend, this is the last chapter of Jeremiah, and it's a heavy one. Zedekiah becomes king of Judah at twenty-one, and he reigns in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother is Hamutal, from Libnah.

cards.question: Zedekiah is on the throne in Jerusalem. How does his reign look in the sight of the LORD?

answers.text: He does evil just like Jehoiakim
He tears down idols like Josiah
He seeks the LORD like Hezekiah

cards.text: Jehoiakim was an earlier king of Judah (2 Kings 23:36), and Zedekiah walks the same road. The text says all this happened because of the anger of the LORD, until He finally banished them from His presence.

cards.question: On top of all that, Zedekiah also rebels against the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Friend, you don't rebel against the king of Babylon and get a polite email back. In Zedekiah's ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marches on Jerusalem with his ENTIRE army.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar's army camps right outside Jerusalem. What do they build all the way around the city?
The siege of Jerusalem lasts until Zedekiah's ___ year, and a ___ grows so severe that the people of the land have no food.

cards.text: Then the city is breached. The Chaldeans, Babylon's army, have Jerusalem surrounded on every side.

cards.question: Jerusalem is breached and the Chaldeans have it surrounded. What do Judah's men of war do?

answers.text: They flee the city by night

cards.text: They slip out through the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, and head toward the Arabah. That's leaving the party without saying goodbye, except it's the WHOLE army.

cards.question: The Chaldeans let King Zedekiah get away into the Arabah.

cards.text: They catch Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and his whole army deserts him. One minute you've got an army, and the next it's just you and a WHOLE lot of footsteps going the other way.

cards.question: The Chaldeans seize King Zedekiah. Where do they bring him to face the king of Babylon?

cards.text: At Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon pronounces judgment on Zedekiah. Friend, this next part is hard to hear.
There at Riblah, the king of Babylon slaughters Zedekiah's sons right before his eyes.

cards.question: At Riblah, the king of Babylon spares the officials of Judah.
The king of Babylon puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him in bronze shackles and keeps him in custody in ___ until his dying day.

cards.text: Zedekiah is gone, but Babylon isn't done with Jerusalem. On the tenth day of the fifth month, Nebuzaradan enters the city. He's captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon.

cards.question: Nebuzaradan is inside Jerusalem. What does he do to the house of the LORD?
Nebuzaradan leaves the royal palace and the houses of Jerusalem standing.

cards.text: The palace, every house, every significant building, all of it burns. Then the Chaldean army breaks down all the walls around Jerusalem.

cards.question: With Jerusalem's walls down, Nebuzaradan gathers people still left in the city. What does he do with them?

answers.text: He puts them to work on the walls
He sends them off to Egypt

cards.text: Some of the poorest people, whoever's left in the city, the deserters who went over to Babylon and the rest of the craftsmen. All of them carried away.

cards.question: Nebuzaradan leaves some of the poorest of the land behind to tend the vineyards and fields.

cards.text: Then the Chaldeans strip the house of the LORD: the two huge bronze pillars with their bronze pomegranates, the stands, the bronze Sea King Solomon made, and the bowls and lampstands of bronze, gold and silver. The weight of all that bronze is beyond measure.
The captain of the guard takes people too: Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank and the three doorkeepers.

cards.question: From the people still in Jerusalem, Nebuzaradan also takes a court official over the men of ___ and seven trusted royal advisers.
Nebuzaradan brings Judah's priests and leaders, along with a scribe and sixty men from the city, to the king of Babylon. Where does he bring them?
The king of Babylon has Judah's priests and leaders at Riblah. What does he do to them?

cards.text: Then the text sums it all up: "So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land."
Before the chapter ends, there's a count of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried away. It comes in three groups over the years, and in all, 4,600 people are taken away.

Now jump to the thirty-seventh year of exile for Jehoiachin, a king of Judah who was carried off to Babylon years before (2 Kings 24:15). Babylon has a new king, Evil-merodach, in the first year of his reign.

cards.question: Evil-merodach is in his first year as king of Babylon. What does he do for Jehoiachin king of Judah?

answers.text: He pardons him and frees him from prison
He moves him to a harsher prison
He puts him on trial all over again

cards.text: Out of prison, after thirty-seven years of exile. And I thought I had it rough in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: Evil-merodach speaks ___ to Jehoiachin and sets his throne ___ the thrones of the other kings with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin changes out of his prison clothes. Where does he dine regularly now?
The king of Babylon gives Jehoiachin a daily portion for just one year.

cards.text: A daily portion for the rest of his life, until the day of his death. After all that fire and ruin, Jeremiah's book ends with a king of Judah out of his prison clothes and eating at the king's table.

findings.problem: The question says the people of the land have no food. That rules out the wrong answers "plague" and "fever" for the second blank, so "famine" is handed to the baker instead of reasoned out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences, but it isn't the walkthrough's opening card. Only the opening card may run to three sentences. Every other story card is limited to one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He sends them off to Egypt" is close in meaning to the right answer "He carries them into exile". Being sent off to a foreign land is a form of exile, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 3 (Jehoiachin is out of prison after thirty-seven years of exile) and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so the joke isn't riding on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
